$comment: HA-3B: the expand/migrate/contract register.
A migration that ships in release N must never make an N-1 replica unsafe
while N-1 remains inside the supported rolling-upgrade window. Adding a
column, table, or index is safe: an old replica simply ignores it. Removing
or narrowing one is not, because an old replica is still reading and writing
the thing being taken away.
check:schema-compat therefore rejects any contracting statement in
backend/drizzle that is not registered here. Registering an entry is the
explicit assertion that no supported replica still depends on the surface,
which is the step the discipline exists to force someone to think about.
The normal shape of a rename is three releases:
N     expand   add `bar`; write both; backfill `foo` -> `bar`
N+1   migrate  every supported replica reads `bar`; nothing depends on `foo`
N+2   contract drop `foo`, registered below
Fields:
migration    the migration file stem, e.g. "0071_bold_husk"
dialect      "sqlite" | "pg" | "both"
surface      the column/table/index being contracted
expandedIn   the release that introduced the replacement surface
approvedFor  the release this contraction may ship in
owner        who asserted the window had passed
justification why no supported replica still reads the surface

rollingUpgradeWindow.note: One HA protocol version. A release that breaks N-1 must bump HA_PROTOCOL_VERSION in backend/src/lib/ha-protocol.ts rather than relying on its release number.
